historic_warning: A historic sheet under this network is a BACKDROP AND NOT EVIDENCE. Stage 1 is a modern river network and makes no historical claim whatever: nothing drawn on it is dated, and a channel lying over an 1890s sheet is not thereby attested in the 1890s. The backdrops are here to read the ground against, and for the stages that will make dated claims — not to let this one imply a claim it does not make. Re-use terms for these layers are not established and no sheet image may be published until they are.
_no_keys: EVERY BACKDROP HERE IS KEYLESS, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE FILE RATHER THAN A CONFIGURATION. The local viewer injects a key from a gitignored .env at request time; a published site has no server to do that, so a keyed entry could only work by shipping the key — and Pages is public even though the repository is not, so a published key can be rotated but never withdrawn. The keyed options are therefore removed from this copy rather than left present and disabled: an entry that can only ever fail is an invitation to make it work. Dropped here: carto_dark, carto_light, nls_six_inch_maptiler. ONE OF THOSE THREE WAS DROPPED FOR A DIFFERENT REASON FROM THE OTHER TWO, and the difference matters. `nls_six_inch_maptiler` is the National Library of Scotland's own Historic Maps API layer — Great Britain, Ordnance Survey six-inch to the mile (1:10,560), 1888-1913 — which is CC BY 3.0, states “You can embed the map in your own website”, and has a free non-commercial tier. It is the sanctioned public route, and it is licensed for exactly this use. It is absent here because of the key, not because of the licence, and it should not be remembered as though the licence objection in _removed_nls applied to it. That objection is about the S3 layers. The first edition has no equivalent route: the API carries no first-edition six-inch at all. Corrected by rewt-86.
_labels: Generated labels show the Library's own tileset identifier verbatim in parentheses. A number in an identifier is not a date and must not be rendered as one: `air-photos-1250` is a scale of 1:1250, whose bucket siblings are 2500 and 10560, and it read as thirteenth-century beside an epoch selector. Only the hand-written labels carry dates, and those are claims someone can be held to.
_removed_nls: EVERY NATIONAL LIBRARY OF SCOTLAND LAYER HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM THE PUBLISHED VIEWER, and the removal is the point rather than an omission. NLS state of the georeferenced layers: 'Re-use of these layers is intended within a desktop or local environment. If you wish you present these layers online in a public website, please use our Historic Maps API layers, or contact us at maps@nls.uk.' This site is public. The Library's own per-layer re-use table lists 29 of 34 layers as CC-BY and does NOT list the England-and-Wales six-inch, one-inch or 25-inch that this viewer drew, so there is no stated term permitting them here either. 68 layers removed. They remain in tools/viewer/, which is the desktop and local environment the Library's sentence describes, and the sanctioned public route is the Historic Maps API — which carries no first-edition six-inch at all, so it is not a substitute. Nothing historic is drawn here until someone has asked maps@nls.uk. REMOVING THE LAYERS WAS NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the part of this worth keeping. After every layer had gone from this file, composite.js still held the base URL of the England-and-Wales six-inch bucket and counties.json still enumerated the 53 slugs that complete it, so the published site continued to carry an index to the removed layers with a working fetcher attached. Each file looked harmless on its own, which is why the first pass missed it. Both are now deleted from docs/ and kept in tools/viewer/, gitignored. Found by rewt-86 on review, not by the agent that did the removal.
